name: Pleione
description: A star 117 parsecs away, 5.7 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17851: radius 5.695 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 94.567 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.602) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17851: effective temperature 7548 +/- 2496 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.495)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17851: distance 117.096 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.036), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 117 parsecs away, 5.7 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 95 times the Sun's luminosity at 7,548 K, so 5.695 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 17851: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Pleione (star)
quotes.card: It has the variable star designation BU Tauri and the Flamsteed designation 28 Tauri.
quotes.introduction: Pleione is located close on the sky to the brighter star Atlas, so is difficult for stargazers to distinguish with the naked eye despite being a fifth magnitude star.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 66529975427235712 (quality A), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
